extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and prosecuting patent claims under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) / pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph — focusing on the two separate requirements (subjective identification of the inventor's claimed invention and objective definiteness of claim scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must set forth the subject matter the inventor regards as the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: “the claims must set forth the subject matter that the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a subjective requirement because it depends on what the inventor(s) regards as his or her invention. The inquiry during examination is patentability of the invention as the inventor or a joint inventor regards it. If claims do not claim what the inventor regards as the invention, the appropriate action is to reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph. (See discussion referencing pre-AIA phrasing and inventor naming under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.41(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must particularly point out and distinctly define the metes and bounds of the subject matter to be protected
rubrics_metrics.description: “the claims must particularly point out and distinctly define the metes and bounds of the subject matter to be protected by the patent grant.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an objective requirement evaluated by whether the claim is definite — i.e., whether the scope of the claim is clear to a hypothetical person possessing the ordinary level of skill in the pertinent art. Failure to meet this requirement supports a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre-AIA second paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definiteness standard: clarity to a person of ordinary skill in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Definiteness is judged by whether the scope of the claim is clear to a hypothetical person possessing the ordinary level of skill in the pertinent art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating definiteness, the examiner should consider how clear the claim scope would be to PHOSITA. The second requirement is objective (not dependent on the inventor's views) and should be applied consistently to remove uncertainties of claim scope during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be precise, clear, correct, and unambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: “Another essential purpose of patent examination is to determine whether or not the claims are precise, clear, correct, and unambiguous.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncertainties of claim scope should be removed, as much as possible, during the examination process. Examiners should aim to resolve ambiguities through office actions and rejections where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When issuing a 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection, explain the basis (indefiniteness vs failure to claim inventor's invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: “If a rejection is based on 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner should further explain whether the rejection is based on indefiniteness or on the failure to claim what the inventor or a joint invention regards as the invention.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for examiners: when making a rejection under 112(b)/pre-AIA second paragraph, state clearly whether the problem is that the claim is indefinite (objective deficiency) or fails to claim the inventor's subjective invention. Cite appropriate authority and factual basis (e.g., In re Zletz; Ex parte Ionescu) as needed.
